t: Subsection (d) of section 806 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92; 10 U.S.C. 2302 note) is amended to read as follows:“(d) Notification Requirement.—Not later than 10 days after exercising the waiver authority under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to Congress providing the details of the waiver and the expected benefits it provides to the Department of Defense.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a formal notification requirement is a participation procedure. But the notification runs from the Secretary of Defense to Congress, both inside the federal government, and it occurs after the waiver is already exercised. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or given a right to object or sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to Congress providing the details of the waiver and the expected benefits it provides to the Department of Defense.

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify Congress about a waiver. Congress is part of the federal government, so this is an intra-governmental notification, not participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to or notifications of Congress.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to Congress providing the details of the waiver and the expected benefits it provides to the Department of Defense.

opus.w: The only procedure here is that the Secretary of Defense must tell Congress after using a waiver. That interaction stays entirely within the federal government. No state, company, expert or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing or right to sue. A formal notification step may look procedural, but reports to Congress fall under the listed exclusions.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to Congress providing the details of the waiver and the expected benefits it provides to the Department of Defense.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, and notifications or reports to Congress are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. Therefore, this intra-governmental communication does not constitute participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to Congress providing the details of the waiver and the expected benefits it provides to the Department of Defense
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that notifying Congress involves "participation" because it is a formal procedural step involving another branch of government. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government, and reports to Congress are a common trap that results in a "No" label.
